task: Several regional governors have raised private armies under the pretext of local defence, and their forces now collectively outnumber the standing national army. The central government's tax collectors and judicial officers are being turned away at provincial borders. One governor has begun minting coins bearing his own insignia, and another has negotiated a separate truce with a neighbouring power without central authorisation. The state risks permanent fragmentation if this trend continues unchecked. Design a strategy to restore central military authority that combines political incentives, targeted enforcement, and institutional reforms, while avoiding a multi-front civil war that the centre cannot currently win.

dispatches.responsibility: Draft the master edict integrating political incentives (amnesty tiers, title confirmations), phased enforcement triggers, and institutional reforms into a single coherent strategy document
Review the drafted strategy for legality, fiscal feasibility, and civil-war escalation risk; exercise seal-and-reject on any provision that would unify all governors against the centre simultaneously
Coordinate execution sequencing across ministries, assign deliverables with timelines, and establish inter-ministry reporting channels for the phased reintegration campaign
Design military posture: concentrate central forces rather than dispersing them, secure strategic chokepoints, and plan targeted enforcement operations against isolated non-compliant governors
Execute fiscal strangulation: redirect tax revenues away from private armies, restore central collection mechanisms, and design economic incentives for compliant governors
Establish legal thresholds defining rebellion vs. legitimate local defence, issue targeted warrants against specific ringleaders, and provide juridical cover for selective enforcement
Control personnel levers: design reinstatement, transfer, and replacement pathways for governors as political incentive, ensuring loyalty-based appointment authority returns to the centre
